product.schneider-eurosx20.summary: The 20 MHz configuration of the EuroSX desktop.
product.schneider-eurosx20.history: In May 1992, IFS advertised the EuroSX /20–90 in Portugal alongside the /16–40 and Euro486. It was the faster-clocked EuroSX configuration, with its own CPU board part number in Schneider’s manual.
product.schneider-eurosx20.technical.con: The advertisement names this offer /20–90. The manual distinguishes the 20 MHz board by part number 53 456 00. The disk drive in this offer still needs comparison with a physical specimen.
product.schneider-eurosx20.technical.boa: The board integrates memory logic and video. The manual shows VLSI VL82C331, BIGJIM at U33 and ATI 28800 at U45. It distinguishes the 16 and 20 MHz boards.
product.schneider-eurosx20.technical.fir: The ROM is split across two chips. The manual identifies LOW and HIGH at U9 and U10. A boot photograph of a EuroSX shows system BIOS 1.05 and VGA 3.01a. These versions still need to be matched to a specific configuration and the dumps preserved.
product.schneider-eurosx20.technical.ver: BluMach has a documentary sheet. A dedicated model and boot validation remain pending.
product.schneider-eurosx20.technical.lim: System and video dumps and comparison of the board map are pending. A photograph suitable for publication is still needed.
product.schneider-eurosx20.technical.man: Schneider, Service Manual EURO 386 SX / L 386/16
